## What is a story?

```{r}
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=20))

ag_production <- read_csv("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/nz/ag_production.csv")
population <- read_csv("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/nz/nz_population.csv")
```

[A story is a collection of facts, observations or events&nbsp;]{.fragment}[ presented in a specific order&nbsp;]{.fragment}[ such that they create an **emotional reaction**.]{.fragment}

## Every story has an arc

:::{.fragment}
**Opening**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Challenge**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Action**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Resolution**
:::

:::{.fragment}
(Challenge and resolution are the most important parts.)
:::

## Wood working as a story

::: {.fragment}
**Opening:** We used to have some cheap poorly built furniture.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Challenge:** Buying well built furniture that we like is expensive.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Action:** I buy some ~~toys~~ tools and learn to build things out of nice timber.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Resolution:** We still buy cheap, poorly built furniture until I get round to it.
:::

## Story structures: newspaper articles

:::{.fragment}
**Lead**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Development**
:::

## Woodworking in this format

:::{.fragment}
**Lead:** Because I'm sick of poorly built furniture, I spent a bunch of money on tools and learnt to build things.
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Development:** I started simple with just a couple of tools and bought laminated panels to build a bookshelf.
:::

:::{.fragment}
But I soon realised that building with recycled native timber didn't just meet a need: it was also a new hobby with lots to learn, lots of toys to play with and lots of fun during building and enjoyment afterwards.
:::

## Story structures: the action movie

:::{.fragment}
**Action**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Background**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Development**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Climax**
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Ending**
:::

## Woodworking in this format

:::{.fragment}
**Action:** In 2000 I bought some ~~toys~~ tools: a router and belt sander.
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Background:** I wanted something nicer than my crappy second hand bed.
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Development:** Over the years I acquired more ~~toys~~ tools and got better at the craft, building all the things.
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Climax:** I completed our shiny new kitchen in 2025.
:::

:::{.fragment}
**Ending:** There's still lots to do: our dining table is intended for camping and the chairs are plastic.
:::


# Telling a story with figures

## Example: Sheep numbers

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
base <- ag_production |>
  filter(animal == "Sheep") |>
  mutate(value = value/1e6) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x=year, y=value) +
  geom_line(col='royalblue', linewidth=1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,71), expand = c(0, 0.03), breaks=seq(0,70,by=10)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0.05)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20) +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Millions of sheep") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())
base
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Challenge**: why the drop?]{.absolute right=20 top=150}
:::

## Example: Sheep numbers

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
base +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1985.5, col='grey50', linewidth=4,
             alpha=0.5) +
  annotate('text', x=1985.5, y=3, label="Farmer subsidies removed", hjust=-0.03,
           col='grey50')

```

:::{.fragment}
[**Resolution**: Government reform]{.absolute right=0 bottom=200}
:::

## Example: Penguins

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
ggplot(penguins) +
  aes(x=bill_len, y=bill_dep) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5, col='grey40') +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', se = FALSE, linewidth=1, linetype='dashed', col='grey40') +
  labs(x="Bill length (mm)", y="Bill depth (mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20)
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Challenge**: decreasing trend?]{.absolute right=10 bottom=150}
:::


## Example: Penguin species

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
ggplot(penguins) +
  aes(x=bill_len, y=bill_dep, col=species) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', se = FALSE, linewidth=1, linetype='dashed', col='grey70') +
  labs(x="Bill length (mm)", y="Bill depth (mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("#E69F00","#0072B2","#009E73")) +
  guides(col='none')
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Challenge**: hmmm...]{.absolute right=10 bottom=150}
:::

## Example: Penguin species

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
ggplot(penguins) +
  aes(x=bill_len, y=bill_dep, col=species, group=species) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', se = FALSE, linewidth=1, linetype='dashed') +
  labs(x="Bill length (mm)", y="Bill depth (mm)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("#E69F00","#0072B2","#009E73")) +
  guides(col='none')
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Resolution**: increasing!]{.absolute right=10 bottom=150}
:::

## Example: Preprints in biology

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
arxiv <- read_csv(here::here("data/arxiv_submissions.csv"))
labels <- arxiv |> slice_max(date) |>
  filter(archive != "bioRxiv")
arxiv |>
  filter(archive != "bioRxiv") |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x=date, y=count) +
  geom_line(colour = 'steelblue') +
  geom_text(data = labels, mapping=aes(label = archive), hjust=-0.1, vjust=0.5, col='steelblue') +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(30, 1500), expand = c(0, 0.03)) +
  scale_x_date(expand=c(0,0.05)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(r = 2, unit="inch"),
        plot.caption = element_text(size=rel(0.6))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip='off') +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Pre-prints per month",
       caption="Data from Claus Wilke's Fundamentals of Data Visualization")
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Challenge**: why the flat line?]{.absolute right=10 bottom=150}
:::

## Example: Preprints in biology

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
arxiv <- read_csv(here::here("data/arxiv_submissions.csv")) |>
  filter(count > 0)
labels <- arxiv |> slice_max(date)
arxiv |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x=date, y=count, col=archive) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_text(data = labels, mapping=aes(label = archive), hjust=-0.1, vjust=0.5) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(30, 1500), expand = c(0, 0.03)) +
  scale_x_date(expand=c(0,0.05)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c('steelblue', 'brown')) +
  guides(colour = 'none') +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(r = 2, unit="inch"),
        plot.caption = element_text(size=rel(0.6))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip='off') +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Pre-prints per month",
       caption="Data from Claus Wilke's Fundamentals of Data Visualization")
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Resolution**: A competitor emerged]{.absolute right=0 bottom=100}
:::

## Example: Egg prices

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
eggs <- read_csv(here::here("data/eggs.csv"))
labels <- eggs |> slice_max(month)
base <- eggs |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x=month, y=price, col=product, group=product) +
  geom_line(col='black', linewidth=1.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth=1) +
  geom_text(data = labels, mapping=aes(label = product), hjust=-0.1, vjust=0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 13.5), expand = c(0, 0.03), labels=scales::label_dollar()) +
  scale_x_date(expand=c(0,0.05)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c('black', 'gold')) +
  guides(colour = 'none') +
  theme_minimal(base_size=20) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(r = 2, unit="inch"),
        plot.caption = element_text(size=rel(0.6))) +
  coord_cartesian(clip='off') +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Price per dozen",
       caption="Free range price scaled from 6 pack to equivalent dozen assuming two free eggs\nReproduced chart from David Hood (@thoughtfulnz.bsky.social)")
base
```

:::{.fragment}
[**Challenge**: big price jump?]{.absolute right=0 top=400}
:::

## Example: Egg prices

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: 'center'
labels <- eggs |> slice_max(month)
base +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ymd('2023-01-01'), col='grey50', linewidth=4,
             alpha=0.5) +
  annotate('text', x=ymd('2023-01-01'), y=1, label="Battery caging banned", hjust=-0.03,
           col='grey50')

```

:::{.fragment}
[**Resolution**: why did it<br />affect free range?!?]{.absolute right=10 top=400}
:::

## Telling a story with figures

Keep in mind that

::: {.incremental}
- Every figure needs a clear purpose within the arc of the story (e.g. challenge, response).

- A complete arc is difficult with just one figure! Usually requires at least two.

- Stories work best in presentations or a series of figures in an article.

- Simpler figures are better as simple stories are easier to grasp.
:::

# Labelling

## Labelling

One of the ways we can help tell stories is with labels and annotation.

:::{.fragment}
Axis and guide labels need to be descriptive.
:::

:::{.fragment}
```{r}
#| eval: false
my_plot + labs(x = NULL, # no need for an x label for dates/years/labelled categories
               y = "My y axis scale (units)",
               colour = "Colour guide")
```
:::

:::{.fragment}
Items within guides need to be descriptive as well!
:::

:::{.fragment}
Either change in the data or use the `labels` parameter in `scale_*()`:
```{r}
#| eval: false
my_plot + scale_colour_manual(labels = c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"))
```
:::


## Labelling example

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
```{r gg9}
#| eval: false
ggplot(data=ag_production) +
  aes(x=year, y=value, colour=animal) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Year",
       y = "Number of animals",
       colour = "Animal")
```

The `labs()` command allows you to override the default labels.

The parameters it takes are the same as aesthetics.

:::

::: {.column .absolute top=0 right=-5%}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| ref.label: "gg9"
```
:::

::::

## Label dictionaries

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
```{r gg10}
#| eval: false

labels = c(year = "Year",
           animal = "Animal",
           value = "Number of Animals")

ggplot(data=ag_production) +
  aes(x=year, y=value, colour=animal) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(dictionary = labels)
```

A label dictionary is a named vector mapping the columns
in your data to the label you want to use.

This can be useful for consistency across multiple plots.
:::

::: {.column .absolute top=0 right=-5%}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| ref.label: "gg10"
```
:::

::::

::: aside
Recall the `c()` function combines multiple entries into a single vector.
:::

## Titles, captions

Titles, subtitles and captions are an opportunity to provide context or story.

:::{.fragment}
```{r}
#| eval: false
my_plot + labs(title = "Gap between people and sheep rapidly closing",
               subtitle = "Sheep:Human ratio over time in Aotearoa New Zealand",
               caption = "Data from Figure.NZ")
```
:::

:::{.fragment}
Editorialising in figure titles is useful to help direct the reader to the key story idea.
:::

## Annotations

:::{.fragment}
`annotate()` can be used to add a single label or other geometry to a chart.
:::

:::{.fragment}
`geom_vline()` and `geom_hline()` are also useful for pointing out key points.
:::

:::{.fragment}
Both of these often require a bit of tuning to get the position correct.
:::

:::{.fragment}
```{r}
#| eval: false
plot +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ymd('2023-01-01'),
             colour='grey50', linewidth=4,
             alpha=0.5) +
  annotate('text', x=ymd('2023-01-01'), y=1,
           label="Battery caging banned", hjust=-0.03,
           colour='grey50')
```
:::
